top_choice_rationale: Adonis (P002) is my first choice on the common criteria. The claim is a distinctive voice and a formal and linguistic achievement that reaches a whole literary language. Through myth, fragmentation and a sustained dialogue with inherited forms, the poetry has remade Arabic poetic language, as shown by Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses. The oeuvre is long enough to be fully formed. I would word the citation narrowly, crediting the poetry alone and treating the essays as a companion strand that is not named. It should make no claim about sound or meter, which I cannot test. The main weakness is that I know the Arabic poetry only through translation and reception. I cannot verify that the later collections sustain the early landmarks. The round-2 exchange also made clear that the Cărtărescu claim (P001) can be tested more directly through translated prose, and that Sward's agreement with me is not independent evidence. That is why Cărtărescu is a very close second and not a lower alternative. I rank him above no award because his architecture of memory, body and dream in Blinding and Solenoid is a serious, distinctive achievement. I rank P000 last because both lead proposals can be given a precise citation, and the open questions concern verification, not distinctiveness. I have not independently verified any source, and my simulated vote as a co-opted member is a modeling assumption.
